questions.q: What does Goins mean by practicing in public?
a: Sharing work openly to gain feedback and an audience
Rehearsing alone until the work is perfect
Performing only at paid private events
Publishing everything under a pen name
questions.why: Lesson 1 says publishing as you go builds a following and brings feedback you cannot get alone.

questions.q: Which two mistakes does the summary warn new artists about?
a: Working for free and selling lifetime rights
Charging too much and hiring an agent
Showing work early and taking feedback
Building an audience and raising prices
questions.why: Lesson 2 warns against not charging at all and against trading one payment for lifetime returns.

questions.q: What should you do when offered exposure instead of payment?
a: Ask for hard numbers before agreeing
Accept it to build your portfolio
Trade it for a public review
Offer to work at a discount
questions.why: Lesson 2 says to demand real audience numbers, because vague exposure is usually a bad deal.

questions.q: What does Goins call today's opportunity for artists?
a: The New Renaissance
The Creative Economy
The Golden Age
The Artist's Return
questions.why: Lesson 3 borrows the Renaissance idea of patrons and applies it to modern creators.

questions.q: Why does the summary say artists should embrace many trades?
a: Multiple income streams let them support their own work
It guarantees representation in a gallery
It removes the need to find an audience
It keeps their art free of commercial pressure
questions.why: Lesson 3 says the new era rewards a jack of all trades who can become their own patron.
